dataset: Three synthetic unseen schemas covering classification, regression and ranking.
decision_reason: The candidate aligns the unknown-family path with the official heterogeneous-column contract, improves deterministic feature visibility and retrieval across all three target types, bounds prompt growth, adds no request cost, and preserves every public answer byte-for-byte.
decision_rule: Require scalar visibility and correct top-1 retrieval for all three target types, 1000-character string bounding, nested-value exclusion, unchanged known-family projection, and byte-identical public outputs.
hypothesis: Unknown-family rows need bounded categorical, boolean and text scalar features in both the model packet and lexical query; numeric-only projection silently removes official input types.
layer: L2 unknown-family input projection and retrieval
limitations: Synthetic schema robustness evidence only; no real-outcome predictive improvement is claimed.
Later scalar fields may be omitted after the 64-field or 6000-character budget.
Arbitrary unknown-classification label semantics remain unsolved.

model_api.reason: The hypothesis concerns deterministic feature visibility, retrieval and boundedness; model output cannot distinguish the input-layer mechanism.

not_measured: Predictive quality; this experiment isolates input and retrieval reachability for previously unseen schemas.

official_references.finding: Entity tables can mix numeric, categorical and text features; most hidden families have no published counterpart.
Rows carry heterogeneous feature columns and the target schema determines classification, regression or ranking output.

public_ab.gate_inference: Byte-identical to the current committed baseline whose 11 public outputs already have recorded smoke and official local NLI evidence; no new smoke or NLI result is claimed.
